correctness.rationale: For any ordered tuple, injectivity of a bimorphism fixes its equality partition, and orientation-preserving homomorphism can only change a missing edge to a chosen directed edge. Conversely each coordinatewise fork extension is a finite injective homomorphism, extended globally by Coleman's MB-homogeneity theorem for the countable generic oriented digraph. Mutual forward reachability is therefore finite induced-pattern equality. Products of V={0<+,0<-} have 3^N elements, 5^N ordered comparable pairs, 2N3^(N-1) covers, rank (1+2q)^N, and Boolean intervals with mu=(-1)^rankdiff. Summation over Stirling-number equality partitions proves all formulas for n>=1. Independent finite tuple-pattern enumeration checks the fork interval counts; the global extension relies on the published theorem, not code.
